component.name: MCP TOOL RUNNER (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
component.description:
What it does Gives an orchestration or an agent access to every tool registered on the organization's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. It calls one tool by name with arguments and returns its result, or lists the tools the server offers together with their descriptions and argument schemas.

How it works The node connects to the organization's own MCP server, which is deployed in Infrastructure like Redis or Milvus. It reads the server's tool list first, so a name the server does not offer comes back as a result with success false and the names that are available, rather than as an opaque failure. A tool that reports an error is also returned with success false and the error text, so an agent can correct its arguments and try again. An MCP server that is not running, or a bad setting, fails the run.

Configure
- Default Tool - the tool to call when the incoming data names none; leave it empty to choose at runtime.
- When No Tool Is Given - list_available (default) returns the tool list; error fails the run.

In and out In: optional tool_name, arguments (an object matching the tool's input schema) and list_tools. Out: success, tool_name, result (the tool's result object, tools when listing, or available_tools when the name was not found) and error.

Use it when
- An agent needs to discover and call tools hosted on the organization's MCP server.
- An orchestration step should run one specific MCP tool with arguments built upstream.
- You want to check which MCP tools are available before wiring them in.
component.short_description: Calls a tool on the organization's MCP server by name, or lists the tools it offers.

declarations.name: default_tool_name
declarations.label: Default Tool
declarations.description: The tool to call when request_data gives no tool_name. Leave empty to choose at runtime.

declarations.name: list_on_empty
declarations.label: When No Tool Is Given
declarations.description: list_available returns the server's tools; error fails the run.

component.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: tool
name: MCP Tool Runner
description: >
  Calls one tool registered on the organization's MCP server, by name and
  with arguments, or lists the tools the server offers. A tool error or an
  unknown tool is returned as data with success false; an MCP server that is
  not running fails the run.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    # A TOOL reached by an INVOKE edge, or a step in a flow. The result is
    # data, not an artifact, so both halves are none.
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    request_data:
      tool_name: string (optional) - The MCP tool to call; overrides Default Tool.
      arguments: object (optional) - Arguments matching the tool's input schema.
      list_tools: boolean (optional) - When true, list the available tools instead of calling one.
    response_data:
      success: boolean - True when the tool ran (or the list was read) without error.
      tool_name: string - The tool that was called; empty when listing.
      result: object - The tool's result (a non-object result as value), or tools when listing, or available_tools when the tool was not found.
      error: string - Why success is false; empty otherwise.

input_parameters:
  - name: default_tool_name
    type: text
    label: Default Tool
    description: The tool to call when request_data gives no tool_name. Leave empty to choose at runtime.
  - name: list_on_empty
    type: select
    label: When No Tool Is Given
    options: [list_available, error]
    default: list_available
    description: list_available returns the server's tools; error fails the run.

tool_name.description: The MCP tool to call; overrides Default Tool.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the tool's input schema.

list_tools.description: When true, list the available tools instead of calling one.

success.description: True when the tool ran (or the list was read) without error.

tool_name.description: The tool that was called; empty when listing.

result.description: The tool's result (a non-object result as value), or tools when listing, or available_tools when the tool was not found.

error.description: Why success is false; empty otherwise.
